title: Bavuma's 179 Leads Record South Africa Fightback Against Australia
excerpt: From 110 for 6, South Africa declared at 425 for 9 at Gqeberha behind their captain's career-best, with Jansen and Harmer adding record lower-order stands.
body:
• Temba Bavuma scored 179 off 334 balls, his highest Test score, as South Africa recovered from 110 for 6 to declare at 425 for 9 against Australia at St George's Park.
  • Marco Jansen made 85 in a 132-run seventh-wicket stand and Simon Harmer 82, his maiden Test fifty, in a 183-run eighth-wicket partnership with his captain.
  • Scott Boland took 5 for 81 for Australia; Mitchell Starc's dismissal of Wiaan Mulder was his 450th Test wicket.
  • Bavuma's 179 is the fourth-highest score by a South African captain in a home Test and the second-highest at Gqeberha, behind Herschelle Gibbs' 196 against India in 2001.

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma produced the innings of his career to drag his side from collapse to control on day three of the second Test against Australia at St George's Park, Gqeberha. Bavuma made 179 from 334 balls, with 18 fours and a six, as South Africa — reduced to 110 for 6 — declared at 425 for 9, according to match reporting of the day's play. Times Now reported the knock broke a long-standing captaincy record associated with India's Mohammad Azharuddin and completed a 76-year first.

A recovery in two acts

Bavuma walked in at 12 for 2 on the opening day and was still there as South Africa slipped to 92 for 5 across two rain-affected days. Marco Jansen provided the first support, scoring 85 in a seventh-wicket partnership of 132 that, as Reuters reported at lunch on day three, had already broken the South Africa seventh-wicket record at St George's Park of 89 runs, set against England in 1896. Simon Harmer then added 82 — his maiden Test half-century — in a 183-run eighth-wicket stand that swung the match.

"Times Now reported the knock broke a long-standing captaincy record associated with India's Mohammad Azharuddin and completed a 76-year first."

South Africa's 425 for 9 is the second-highest innings total by a team after losing six wickets for 110 runs or fewer, behind England's 446 against Pakistan at Lord's in 2010. Bavuma reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls before passing his previous best of 172, made against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023.

Where the knock sits in the record books

The 179 is the fourth-highest individual score by a South African captain in a home Test, behind Hashim Amla's 208 against West Indies in 2014, Amla's 201 against England in 2016 and Graeme Smith's 183 against England in 2010. At this ground, only Herschelle Gibbs' 196 against India in 2001 stands above it — a small piece of India-linked history inside a South African record. For Australia, Scott Boland finished with 5 for 81, and Starc's removal of Wiaan Mulder — given out only after review when the batter gloved a short ball behind — was his 450th Test wicket. Australia, who lead the series after the Durban Test, began their reply at 3 for 1. The match continues, with South Africa's captain having turned a probable defeat position into the game's commanding total.

The innings also carried a personal weight for Bavuma, whose captaincy has been questioned through South Africa's home season. He had walked in with the innings at 12 for 2 on a rain-interrupted first day, absorbed the collapse around him across two days, and then accelerated only after the lower order had secured the total — a sequence that turned a survival exercise into the highest score of his Test career and, by the declaration, the defining performance of the series so far.
